correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=5 and positive t, the prism Laplacian splits exactly into cycle and massive cycle blocks, yielding tau=(n/2)det(Lcycle+2D). A rank-three determinant lemma gives the displayed 3x3 kernel. The periodic Green kernel follows from q+1/q=4 and the normalized delta source, and its determinant expansion has exactly the quadratic/cubic terms shown. The balancing difference factors as u^2 c^2(1-q^2)(q^(2x+2)-q^(2y))/q^2 times [1+q^(2z)+(u/sqrt(3))(1-q^(2z))], where u=t-1>-1; all factors are strictly positive for x+1<y and u!=0. Exact integer gap balancing/reverse balancing gives all extremizers and equality cases. Replayed standalone standard-library code completed 14694 exact-rational checks; an independent symbolic expansion confirmed the nonstandard algebraic factors. Finite tests support but do not replace the all-size proof.

value.rationale: A finite engineering/statistical-physics design problem with infinitely many sizes is resolved completely: three specified interlayer bonds of fixed conductance contrast may be placed to maximize or minimize weighted spanning-tree entropy, and both optimal layouts are determined. The third marked rung creates an independent cubic interaction not controlled solely by two-point negative correlation. A nontrivial cancellation gives a uniform positive local-balancing formula for every positive conductance, including weakened links, thereby explaining why the optimizer does not reverse. These are sharp structural all-size statements, not a numerical lookup, parameter rename or routine single-example recomputation.
residual_risks: Practical significance is for three identical vertical defects on circular ladders; a wider-strip extension remains unproved.
No claim that three is the smallest or only defect count exhibiting a distinctive arrangement phenomenon.
